description: Weekly updates: one PR for every non-major update, one per major upgrade, up to five ordinary PRs per repository, and review before every merge.
prHeader: Review required: check dependency impact and CI before merging. One weekly PR carries every non-major update; each major upgrade, Python minor upgrades and lock-file maintenance come as their own PRs. Up to five ordinary PRs are open per repository; queued updates wait for a slot and the next Monday run, and the repository's Dependency Dashboard issue lists them.

logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^Some (release|upgrade)\(s\) did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

lockFileMaintenance.description: Owner rule (2026-10-21), lock files: lock-file maintenance re-resolves every transitive dependency, so the 4-day soak is handed to the package manager. Renovate passes it to npm as --before and to Poetry 2.4+ as POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE. uv, pnpm and bun take it only from the consumer's own setting (exclude-newer, minimumReleaseAge). This never holds the PR itself: lock-file maintenance has no release date, and the stability status check is off. See docs/decisions/0001-fleet-release-age-soak.md.

packageRules.description: group:allNonMajor (extends) puts every minor and patch update into one weekly 'all non-major dependencies' PR. This adds digest, pin and pinDigest updates to the same PR (same groupName and groupSlug). Lock-file maintenance stays its own PR: Renovate 44.107.0 cannot group it with other update types (lib/workers/repository/updates/branch-name.ts). Majors are not matched and come one PR each; later rules (Python, consumer groups) take precedence.
Refresh npm ranges even when the newest eligible version already satisfies the old range.
Keep major upgrades out of the non-major group, one PR each, and preserve Renovate's related-package groups (such as monorepos); never automerge.
Preserve first-party codeOps workflow and action branch refs without digest pinning; retain other update handling

Python (1 of 2): report Python patch updates apart from minor ones, so a patch release (3.14.7 to 3.14.8) is not hidden behind a minor upgrade waiting in the python PR of rule 2. Renovate then puts Python patches in a separate patch branch of the non-major group. No matchUpdateTypes here because Renovate reads separateMinorPatch before an update type exists.

Python (2 of 2): Python minor and major upgrades (such as 3.14 to 3.15) come together in one python PR, majors in their own, outside the non-major group, and are never automerged. Patch, digest and pin updates stay in the non-major group. Matches by package name in every manager: python and other registry python images, setup-python python-version inputs, .python-version, requires-python, runtime.txt, and mise, asdf, proto, devbox, pixi, poetry and devcontainer pins. The setup-python action and the devcontainer python feature are not Python releases and are not matched. Until 2026-10-22 this rule set enabled: false, which hid these upgrades without a PR; that freeze had no owner record and was removed (renovate-config#33).

Owner rule (2026-10-21): every major, minor and patch update (including npm range bumps and lock-file-only updates, which are flags on those) and every digest update waits 4 days after publication before Renovate raises it, in every consumer. timestamp-required (Renovate's default since v42, stated so any consumer override is explicit) also holds an update whose release date is missing, which is right for sources that publish dates: npm, PyPI, crates.io, GitHub releases and tags, Docker Hub, and third-party GHCR images (custom.ghcr, below). Sources that publish no dates are switched to timestamp-optional by the three 'undated sources' rules below (owner, 2026-10-22: no permanent holds), so their updates come as ordinary PRs. Pin, pinDigest, replacement, lockFileMaintenance and rollback updates carry no release date and are not held. Vulnerability-fix PRs bypass this through vulnerabilityAlerts. See docs/decisions/0001-fleet-release-age-soak.md.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), first-party code: first-party GitHub actions, workflows and releases are this fleet's own code, so they do not wait 4 days. Scoped to GitHub datasources so the same names on another registry (for example an unclaimed Docker Hub namespace) still wait. First-party GHCR images need no rule: they are undated and come through under 'undated sources (2 of 3)'.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), GHCR dates: date third-party GHCR images. Renovate's docker datasource reads no dates from ghcr.io. custom.ghcr (customDatasources above) reads tags, index digests and created_at from the GitHub Packages API (GET /users/{owner}/packages/container/{name}/versions, which also serves org-owned packages). GitHub sets created_at when a digest is first pushed; the publisher cannot set it. Needs a runner token with read:packages: without it every lookup fails with HTTP 403, the image gets no update (a lookup warning on the Dependency Dashboard), and the runner's GHCR probe reports it. The API returns one page, the newest 100 versions, including untagged platform manifests and signatures. A release older than that page is invisible, and a pinned tag that has left it gets no digest update ('Could not determine new digest'). Excluded here because 100 versions span hours, so no release would ever be 4 days old in the page (measured 2026-10-21): astral-sh/uv, cloudnative-pg/postgresql and renovatebot/renovate. They and first-party images stay on the docker datasource, undated, and come through under 'undated sources (2 of 3)'. An image whose Docker Hub repository serves the same digests can be referenced there instead, to get Docker Hub dates. After this rule, matchDatasources: [docker] no longer matches the images it moves; match them by name, or list custom.ghcr too. See docs/decisions/0001-fleet-release-age-soak.md.

Owner rule (2026-10-22), undated sources (1 of 3): git-refs, git-tags, github-runners, java-version and dart-version carry no release dates in Renovate 44.107.0, so timestamp-required held their updates forever. timestamp-optional keeps the 4-day wait whenever a date exists and otherwise lets the update through as an ordinary PR for review. python-version is dated from python.org's release feed and so waits 4 days; it is listed so a feed outage does not hold Python patch releases. Replaces the 2026-10-21 exemption of the runtime lists and runner labels, which skipped the wait even when a date existed.

Owner rule (2026-10-22), undated sources (2 of 3): Renovate's docker datasource reads release dates only from Docker Hub (an image name with no registry host, or docker.io, index.docker.io or registry-1.docker.io). Images on every other registry (quay.io, registry.k8s.io, mcr.microsoft.com, lscr.io, first-party ghcr.io images, and the GHCR images the rule above leaves on the docker datasource) were held forever; they now come as ordinary PRs, and wait 4 days if a date ever appears. Must stay after the GHCR rule, so the images it moves to custom.ghcr keep timestamp-required.

Owner rule (2026-10-22), undated sources (3 of 3): a digest update of a tag that is not a version (latest, lts-alpine, stable, or a branch name such as main) has no release to take a date from, so it was held forever, even on Docker Hub. It now comes as an ordinary PR. A versioned tag (1.27, v2.5.0, 3.13-slim) keeps timestamp-required: its digest update is dated by that version's release.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), lock files, part 2: lock-file maintenance runs only for managers whose lock regeneration can honour the 4-day soak. From Renovate: npm gets --before for package-lock.json, and poetry gets POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE, which only Poetry 2.4+ honours (Renovate runs the Poetry version in the poetry.lock header, so an older lock must be re-locked). Consumer-supplied, not checked here: pnpm-workspace.yaml minimumReleaseAge, bunfig.toml minimumReleaseAge, uv exclude-newer in pyproject.toml; a repository without its setting gets un-soaked maintenance. yarn.lock and pdm.lock are handled by part 3. Every other manager re-resolves with no age check: cargo, bundler, composer, gradle, terraform, helmv3 and the rest take the newest release, and nuget, though it resolves the lowest applicable version, takes the newest match for a floating version such as 1.*. Their lock files change only with an ordinary update: the proposed version is soaked, but the transitive releases the package manager re-resolves for it are not.

Owner rule (2026-10-21), lock files, part 3: the npm manager also maintains yarn.lock and the pep621 manager also maintains pdm.lock. Renovate passes no cooldown to Yarn or PDM, and Yarn Classic has none, so lock-file maintenance is off wherever one of those lock files is present (matchFileNames also matches a package file's lock files). A Yarn Berry or PDM repository that sets its own cooldown can turn it back on locally. No fleet repository used either on 2026-10-22.

vulnerabilityAlerts.prHeader: Review required: check dependency impact and CI before merging. This is a security fix: it is not scheduled, not held for release age, and does not use or wait for the repository's five ordinary PR slots.
